claim: The acidic patch is a functionally important epitope on each face of the nucleosome that affects chromatin remodeling.
source: The acidic patch is a functionally important epitope on each face of the nucleosome that affects chromatin remodeling.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general statement about the acidic patch, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: Each acidic patch is uniquely positioned relative to a bound remodeler despite being related by 2-fold symmetry of the nucleosome.
source: Although related by 2-fold symmetry of the nucleosome, each acidic patch is uniquely positioned relative to a bound remodeler.
evidence: This is a structural observation based on nucleosome symmetry and remodeler binding geometry.

claim: The Chd1 remodeler from Saccharomyces cerevisiae and ISWI remodelers from human and Drosophila have distinct spatial requirements for the acidic patch.
source: Here, we use this methodology to show that the Chd1 remodeler from Saccharomyces cerevisiae and ISWI remodelers from human and Drosophila have distinct spatial requirements for the acidic patch.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2-4.

claim: Chd1 is equally affected by entry- and exit-side acidic patch mutations.
source: Unlike Chd1, which is equally affected by entry- and exit-side mutations, ISWI remodelers strongly depend on the entry-side acidic patch.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data in Figure 2 showing similar effects of APM on either side for Chd1.

claim: ISWI remodelers strongly depend on the entry-side acidic patch.
source: Unlike Chd1, which is equally affected by entry- and exit-side mutations, ISWI remodelers strongly depend on the entry-side acidic patch.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Asymmetry in the two acidic patches stimulates ISWI to slide mononucleosomes off DNA ends.
source: Remarkably, asymmetry in the two acidic patches stimulates ISWI to slide mononucleosomes off DNA ends, overriding the remodeler's preference to shift the histone core toward longer flanking DNA.
evidence: This is supported by histone mapping data in Figure 4 showing directional sliding off DNA ends.

claim: Asymmetric acidic patches override ISWI's preference to shift the histone core toward longer flanking DNA.
source: Remarkably, asymmetry in the two acidic patches stimulates ISWI to slide mononucleosomes off DNA ends, overriding the remodeler's preference to shift the histone core toward longer flanking DNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments in Figures 3 and 4 where ISWI slides nucleosomes toward the wild-type acidic patch regardless of DNA length.

claim: SWI/SNF was the first chromatin remodeling family discovered.
source: The first chromatin remodeling family discovered, SWI/SNF, was identified for its ability to promote gene activation by disrupting nucleosomes (Hirschhorn et al., 1992; Kwon et al., 1994; Peterson and Herskowitz, 1992).
evidence: This is a historical fact supported by citations to the original discovery papers.

claim: SWI/SNF was identified for its ability to promote gene activation by disrupting nucleosomes.
source: The first chromatin remodeling family discovered, SWI/SNF, was identified for its ability to promote gene activation by disrupting nucleosomes (Hirschhorn et al., 1992; Kwon et al., 1994; Peterson and Herskowitz, 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the original discovery papers.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers play an opposing role to SWI/SNF by reducing cryptic transcription in gene bodies.
source: In contrast, Chd1 and ISWI remodelers play an opposing role, reducing cryptic transcription in gene bodies by stimulating nucleosome assembly and organizing nucleosomes into evenly-spaced arrays (Ito et al., 1997; Lusser et al., 2005; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers stimulate nucleosome assembly and organize nucleosomes into evenly-spaced arrays.
source: In contrast, Chd1 and ISWI remodelers play an opposing role, reducing cryptic transcription in gene bodies by stimulating nucleosome assembly and organizing nucleosomes into evenly-spaced arrays (Ito et al., 1997; Lusser et al., 2005; Smolle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: SWI/SNF enzymes can slide nucleosomes on top of transcription factors bound to flanking DNA, thereby dissociating them.
source: SWI/SNF enzymes can slide nucleosomes on top of transcription factors bound to flanking DNA, thereby dissociating them, whereas Chd1 and ISWI remodelers preferentially shift nucleosomes away from transcription factors, preserving their occupancy (Dechassa et al., 2010; Kang et al., 2002; Li et al., 2015; Nagaich et al., 2004; Nodelman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers preferentially shift nucleosomes away from transcription factors, preserving their occupancy.
source: SWI/SNF enzymes can slide nucleosomes on top of transcription factors bound to flanking DNA, thereby dissociating them, whereas Chd1 and ISWI remodelers preferentially shift nucleosomes away from transcription factors, preserving their occupancy (Dechassa et al., 2010; Kang et al., 2002; Li et al., 2015; Nagaich et al., 2004; Nodelman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Directional sliding by Chd1 and ISWI is achieved by coupling DNA sensing to DNA translocation by a conserved ATPase motor.
source: Directional sliding by Chd1 and ISWI is achieved by coupling DNA sensing to DNA translocation by a conserved ATPase motor (Flaus et al., 2006; Nodelman et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The ATPase motor can shift nucleosomes by acting at either of the two symmetrically related superhelix location 2 (SHL2) sites.
source: The ATPase motor can shift nucleosomes by acting at either of the two symmetrically related superhelix location 2 (SHL2) sites (McKnight et al., 2011; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: At each SHL2 site, the ATPase motor always shifts DNA toward the nucleosome dyad.
source: At each SHL2 site, the ATPase motor always shifts DNA toward the nucleosome dyad; therefore, action at each site results in DNA movement in opposite directions.
evidence: This is a mechanistic description based on established understanding of remodeler action.

claim: Action at each SHL2 site results in DNA movement in opposite directions.
source: At each SHL2 site, the ATPase motor always shifts DNA toward the nucleosome dyad; therefore, action at each site results in DNA movement in opposite directions.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the motor shifting DNA toward the dyad from two symmetrically related sites.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers show highest sliding activity when DNA is longer and exposed on the entry side and shorter or inaccessible on the exit side.
source: As directional sliding factors, Chd1 and ISWI remodelers show highest sliding activity when DNA is longer and exposed on the entry side and shorter or inaccessible on the exit side (Nodelman et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers possess a similarly folded DNA-binding domain (DBD) that interacts with flanking DNA.
source: Chd1 and ISWI remodelers possess a similarly folded DNA-binding domain (DBD) that interacts with flanking DNA (Dang and Bartholomew, 2007; Grüne et al., 2003; Nodelman et al., 2017; Ryan et al., 2011; Yamada et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published structural and functional studies.

claim: For the DBD to reach entry-side DNA with the ATPase motor simultaneously bound at SHL2, the remodeler has to span across the width of the nucleosome disk.
source: For the DBD to reach entry-side DNA with the ATPase motor simultaneously bound at SHL2, the remodeler therefore has to span across the width of the nucleosome disk.
evidence: This is a geometric inference based on the positions of the DBD binding site and SHL2.

claim: The ATPase subunit of human ISWI remodeler SNF2h and the related ACF complex are sensitive to disruption of the nucleosome acidic patch.
source: Recently, the ATPase subunit of the human ISWI remodeler, called SNF2h, and the related ACF complex were shown in two studies to be sensitive to disruption of the nucleosome 'acidic patch' (Dann et al., 2017; Gamarra et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to two published studies.

claim: The acidic patch is a distinctive cluster of eight acidic residues on H2A and H2B.
source: Recently, the ATPase subunit of the human ISWI remodeler, called SNF2h, and the related ACF complex were shown in two studies to be sensitive to disruption of the nucleosome 'acidic patch' (Dann et al., 2017; Gamarra et al., 2018), a distinctive cluster of eight acidic residues on H2A and H2B that participate in chromatin condensation (Dorigo et al., 2003; Luger et al., 1997; Shogren-Knaak et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a structural description supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The acidic patch participates in chromatin condensation.
source: a distinctive cluster of eight acidic residues on H2A and H2B that participate in chromatin condensation (Dorigo et al., 2003; Luger et al., 1997; Shogren-Knaak et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The acidic patch is used by many chromatin factors for nucleosome recognition and binding.
source: While the acidic patch is also used by many chromatin factors for nucleosome recognition and binding (Kalashnikova et al., 2013; McGinty and Tan, 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Chd1 has only a modest (~2 fold) defect in sliding nucleosomes with acidic patch mutations.
source: Chd1 was found to only have a modest (~2 fold) defect in sliding nucleosomes with acidic patch mutations (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: For experiments with Chd1, only the acidic patch on the entry H2A/H2B dimer was mutated.
source: One key difference in these studies was that for the experiments with Chd1, only the acidic patch on the entry H2A/H2B dimer was mutated, whereas for the ISWI studies, the acidic patch was mutated on both entry and exit dimers.
evidence: This describes the experimental design differences between previous studies.

claim: For ISWI studies, the acidic patch was mutated on both entry and exit dimers.
source: One key difference in these studies was that for the experiments with Chd1, only the acidic patch on the entry H2A/H2B dimer was mutated, whereas for the ISWI studies, the acidic patch was mutated on both entry and exit dimers.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of previous ISWI studies.

claim: Using the Widom 601 nucleosome positioning sequence, hexasomes can be produced in an oriented fashion, where the sole H2A/H2B dimer preferentially deposits on the TA-rich side.
source: We previously showed that, using the Widom 601 nucleosome positioning sequence, hexasomes can be produced in an oriented fashion, where the sole H2A/H2B dimer preferentially deposits on the so-called TA-rich side (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Nucleosomes can be generated from addition of H2A/H2B dimers to hexasomes.
source: Since nucleosomes can be generated from addition of H2A/H2B dimers to hexasomes, oriented hexasomes allows for the homogeneous production of nucleosomes having different mutations or modifications on each H2A/H2B dimer (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Oriented hexasomes allow for homogeneous production of nucleosomes having different mutations or modifications on each H2A/H2B dimer.
source: Since nucleosomes can be generated from addition of H2A/H2B dimers to hexasomes, oriented hexasomes allows for the homogeneous production of nucleosomes having different mutations or modifications on each H2A/H2B dimer (Levendosky et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a methodological statement supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Chd1 is similarly affected by acidic patch mutations on entry and exit H2A/H2B dimers.
source: Whereas Chd1 is similarly affected by acidic patch mutations on entry and exit H2A/H2B dimers, ISWI depends much more strongly on having a wild type acidic patch on the entry dimer.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: ISWI depends much more strongly on having a wild type acidic patch on the entry dimer.
source: Whereas Chd1 is similarly affected by acidic patch mutations on entry and exit H2A/H2B dimers, ISWI depends much more strongly on having a wild type acidic patch on the entry dimer.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Asymmetry in the two acidic patches results in strongly biased sliding of asymmetric nucleosomes by ISWI, with net movement toward the side containing the wild type acidic patch.
source: This dependence results in strongly biased sliding of asymmetric nucleosomes by ISWI, with net movement toward the side containing the wild type acidic patch.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by histone mapping data in Figure 4.

claim: Selective blocking of one acidic patch in vivo would locally redirect ISWI action to disorganize and potentially disrupt nucleosomes.
source: These findings suggest that in vivo, selective blocking of one acidic patch would locally redirect ISWI action to disorganize and potentially disrupt nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The acidic patch mutation (APM) consists of four alanine substitutions on H2A (E61A/E64A/D90A/E92A).
source: The acidic patch mutation (APM) consists of four alanine substitutions on H2A (E61A/E64A/D90A/E92A), highlighted in cyan.
evidence: This is stated in the figure legend and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Chd1 shifted histone octamers away from DNA ends for all eight nucleosomes tested.
source: For all eight nucleosomes, Chd1 shifted histone octamers away from the DNA ends, consistent with nucleosome centering activity.
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: For both 0N80 and 80N0 constructs, nucleosomes containing the double APM/APM were shifted most slowly by Chd1.
source: For both 0N80 and 80N0 constructs, the nucleosomes containing the double APM/APM were shifted most slowly, whereas single APM nucleosomes were only slightly slower than wild type.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Single APM nucleosomes were shifted only slightly slower than wild type by Chd1.
source: For both 0N80 and 80N0 constructs, the nucleosomes containing the double APM/APM were shifted most slowly, whereas single APM nucleosomes were only slightly slower than wild type.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2B-C.

claim: APM on the entry-side dimer had a modest effect on Chd1, slowing down the sliding reaction by ~2 fold.
source: In agreement with our previous findings (Levendosky et al., 2016), APM on the entry-side dimer (adjacent to the 80 bp DNA) had a rather modest effect, slowing down the sliding reaction by ~2 fold (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 2C-D and consistent with previous findings.

claim: Sliding by Chd1 was slowed down (~3 fold) by an APM on the exit side H2A/H2B.
source: Here, we find that sliding was also slowed down (~3 fold) by an APM on the exit side H2A/H2B (adjacent to the zero bp DNA side).
evidence: This is a new finding supported by the data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: APM on both sides of the nucleosome appeared to have an additive effect on Chd1 activity, resulting in 7- to 10-fold slower sliding.
source: Interestingly, APM on both sides appeared to have an additive effect, resulting in 7- to 10-fold slower sliding.
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The sliding rates for 0N80 nucleosomes were faster than 80N0 nucleosomes for Chd1.
source: As we anticipated, the sliding rates for the 0N80 nucleosomes (TA-poor adjacent to 80 bp flanking DNA, Figure 2C, blue bars) was faster than 80N0 nucleosomes (TA-rich adjacent to 80 bp flanking DNA, gray bars).
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 2C.

claim: The relative slow-down due to APM on one or both sides was remarkably similar for 0N80 and 80N0 nucleosomes with Chd1, and therefore relatively unbiased by the underlying DNA sequence.
source: Yet despite these rate differences, the relative slow-down due to APM on one or both sides was remarkably similar, and therefore relatively unbiased by the underlying DNA sequence (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by the normalized data in Figure 2D.

claim: The additive effect of APM on Chd1 implies that either a single remodeler can sense both acidic patches, or possibly that two remodelers on opposite sides of the nucleosome can communicate in a way that is sensitive to the acidic patch.
source: The additive effect of APM implies that either a single remodeler can sense both acidic patches, or possibly that two remodelers on opposite sides of the nucleosome can communicate in a way that is sensitive to the acidic patch.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the additive effect observed in the data.

claim: Disrupting both acidic patches (APM/APM) reduced sliding activity of SNF2h ~200 fold.
source: Previous experiments showed that disrupting both acidic patches (APM/APM) more dramatically reduced sliding activity of SNF2h (~200 fold) compared with ACF (~10 fold) (Gamarra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Disrupting both acidic patches (APM/APM) reduced sliding activity of ACF ~10 fold.
source: Previous experiments showed that disrupting both acidic patches (APM/APM) more dramatically reduced sliding activity of SNF2h (~200 fold) compared with ACF (~10 fold) (Gamarra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The impact of double APM nucleosomes on Chd1 activity was similar to the reduction in the rate of nucleosome centering observed for ACF.
source: Therefore, the impact of the double APM nucleosomes on Chd1 activity was similar to the reduction in the rate of nucleosome centering observed for ACF.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current findings and previous results.

claim: Both SNF2h and ACF shifted APM/APM nucleosomes significantly more slowly than WT/WT nucleosomes.
source: In agreement with previous results (Dann et al., 2017; Gamarra et al., 2018), both SNF2h and ACF shifted APM/APM nucleosomes significantly more slowly than WT/WT nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3A-B and consistent with previous findings.

claim: SNF2h was sensitive to the 601 sequence orientation, sliding both WT/WT and APM/APM nucleosomes more readily in the 0N80 orientation.
source: As observed with Chd1, SNF2h was sensitive to the 601 sequence orientation, sliding both WT/WT and APM/APM nucleosomes more readily in the 0N80 orientation, with the TA-poor side of 601 on the side adjacent to the 80 bp flanking DNA (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3A.

claim: With asymmetrically placed APMs, both SNF2h and ACF showed different behaviors depending on whether the APM was on the 80 bp or 0 bp side.
source: Interestingly, with asymmetrically placed APMs, both SNF2h and ACF showed different behaviors depending on whether the APM was on the 80 bp or 0 bp side.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3A-B.

claim: When the APM was on the 0 bp side, nucleosomes initially moved toward the center but then appeared to shift back toward the DNA ends for SNF2h and ACF.
source: When the APM was on the 0 bp side, nucleosomes initially moved toward the center (up the gel, migrating more slowly) but then appeared to shift back toward the DNA ends (down the gel) (Figure 3A,B, 0N80 APM/WT and 80N0 WT/APM).
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data in Figure 3A-B.

claim: After moving up the gel, the return of nucleosomes to the lower, end position coincided with the emergence of free DNA for SNF2h and ACF.
source: After moving up the gel, the return of nucleosomes to the lower, end position coincided with the emergence of free DNA (highlighted with asterisks).
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data in Figure 3A-B.

claim: For SNF2h, similar increases in free DNA were observed for single APM-containing nucleosomes on the 80 bp side.
source: For SNF2h, similar increases in free DNA were also observed for single APM-containing nucleosomes on the 80 bp side.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3A.

claim: SNF2h was unable to shift nucleosomes with APM on the 80 bp side toward more central locations.
source: These nucleosomes (80N0 APM/WT and 0N80 WT/APM) were different in that they did not yield any slower migrating species, suggesting that SNF2h was unable to shift these toward more central locations.
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data in Figure 3A.

claim: For 80N0 nucleosomes with an APM on the 80 bp side (APM/WT), SNF2h produced a faster migrating species expected for hexasomes.
source: Interestingly, for 80N0 nucleosomes with an APM on the 80 bp side (APM/WT), SNF2h instead produced a faster migrating species expected for hexasomes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data in Figure 3A.

claim: The free DNA species clearly increased over time for both ACF and SNF2h on APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes.
source: When quantified relative to nucleosome bands, the free DNA species clearly increased over time for both ACF and SNF2h on APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 3C.

claim: The strong increase in free DNA was not observed for WT/WT nucleosomes with SNF2h and ACF, indicating that the asymmetry of the acidic patch was essential.
source: The same strong increase was not observed for WT/WT nucleosomes, indicating that the asymmetry of the acidic patch was essential.
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 3C.

claim: A similar increase in free DNA was not observed for Chd1 on APM/WT nucleosomes.
source: A similar increase in free DNA was not observed for Chd1, reinforcing the conclusion that Chd1 and ISWI respond differently to asymmetric APM/WT nucleosomes.
evidence: This is supported by the quantified data in Figure 3C.

claim: FLAG-Acf1 was stably associated with the ATPase subunit in the ACF complex.
source: These control experiments indicate that Acf1 was tightly associated with the ATPase subunit, supporting the notion that the striking sliding behavior of APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes were characteristics of the full ACF complex.
evidence: This is supported by the FLAG pulldown experiments in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The centering-then-decentering behavior of ACF on APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes appeared to be concentration dependent.
source: One observation we made in the course of these experiments was that the centering-then-decentering behavior of ACF on APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes appeared to be concentration dependent.
evidence: This is supported by comparing data at different ACF concentrations in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1-2.

claim: With excess ACF over nucleosomes (100 nM ACF, 40 nM nucleosomes), ACF initially shifted end-positioned nucleosomes toward a more central position, followed by a redistribution toward a DNA end.
source: With excess ACF over nucleosomes (100 nM ACF, 40 nM nucleosomes), ACF initially shifted end-positioned nucleosomes toward a more central position, followed by a redistribution toward a DNA end (Figure 3B, APM/WT).
evidence: This is supported by the native gel data in Figure 3B.

claim: With a limiting amount of ACF (10 nM ACF, 40 nM nucleosomes), only an initial nucleosome shift toward the center was apparent.
source: Yet with a limiting amount of ACF (10 nM ACF, 40 nM nucleosomes), only an initial nucleosome shift toward the center was apparent with a similar time course (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: With extended time points (up to 90 hr) and limiting ACF, the migration pattern clearly showed a redistribution of nucleosomes back toward end positioning.
source: However, this apparent concentration dependence instead may simply reflect a much slower rate of equilibration with undersaturating ACF, because with extended time points (up to 90 hr), the migration pattern clearly showed a redistribution of nucleosomes back toward end positioning (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both human SNF2h and Drosophila ACF are strikingly different from yeast Chd1 in how they remodel asymmetric nucleosomes.
source: These results show that both human SNF2h and Drosophila ACF are strikingly different from yeast Chd1 in how they remodel these asymmetric nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The appearance of free DNA with APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes suggests that SNF2h and ACF can destabilize nucleosomes containing a single APM.
source: Moreover, the appearance of free DNA with APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes suggests that SNF2h and ACF can destabilize nucleosomes containing a single APM.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the free DNA data in Figure 3C.

claim: For nucleosomes containing a single APM, the apparent destabilization and inability to maintain histone octamers in a central location may reflect biased, directional movement of nucleosomes.
source: We suspected that for nucleosomes containing a single APM, the apparent destabilization and inability to maintain histone octamers in a central location may reflect biased, directional movement of nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that motivated the histone mapping experiments.

claim: The native gel sliding experiments were consistent with the histone octamer preferentially moving toward the side possessing the wild type acidic patch.
source: The native gel sliding experiments were consistent with the histone octamer preferentially moving toward the side possessing the wild type acidic patch.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the native gel data in Figure 3.

claim: For symmetric nucleosomes (WT/WT or APM/APM), SNF2h shifted histone octamers to more central locations on the DNA fragment.
source: For the symmetric nucleosomes, which contained either two wild type acidic patches or two APM sites, the histone octamers were shifted by SNF2h to more central locations on the DNA fragment (Figure 4A,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,D).
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4A,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,D.

claim: For asymmetric nucleosomes, the histone octamer always shifted in the direction of the H2A/H2B dimer containing the wild type acidic patch, regardless of flanking DNA length.
source: For the asymmetric nucleosomes, however, the pattern of nucleosome repositioning was quite different. For both 0N80 and 80N0 nucleosomes, the histone octamer always shifted in the direction of the H2A/H2B dimer containing the wild type acidic patch, regardless of flanking DNA length.
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: On 0N80 nucleosomes, SNF2h shifted WT/APM octamers off the zero side by up to 52 bp.
source: On 0N80 nucleosomes, SNF2h shifted WT/APM octamers off the zero side by up to 52 bp (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4B.

claim: For APM/WT 0N80 nucleosomes, SNF2h shifted the histone octamer in the opposite direction, across the entire length of the flanking 80 bp.
source: For the APM/WT nucleosomes, where the wild type and mutated acidic positions are swapped, SNF2h shifted the histone octamer in the opposite direction, across the entire length of the flanking 80 bp (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4C.

claim: For all asymmetric APM/WT and WT/APM nucleosomes, the histone octamer shifted farther than the available flanking DNA.
source: For all asymmetric APM/WT and WT/APM nucleosomes, the histone octamer shifted farther than the available flanking DNA, which means that portions of the DNA-binding surface of the histones became exposed as the DNA end was pulled to a more internal position on the nucleosome.
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The DNA end was shifted up to ~50 bp past the canonical edge of the nucleosome, which corresponds to the internal SHL2 site where the ATPase motor acts.
source: In each case, the DNA end was shifted up to ~50 bp past the canonical edge of the nucleosome, which corresponds to the internal SHL2 site where the ATPase motor acts.
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Movement of the histone octamer off DNA ends was destabilizing and likely responsible for hexasome formation and free DNA.
source: These results are consistent with the native gel sliding experiments (Figure 3), and suggest that movement of the histone octamer off DNA ends was destabilizing and likely responsible for hexasome formation and free DNA.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the histone mapping data to the native gel observations.

claim: SNF2h continued to pull DNA onto the nucleosome even after no entry-side flanking DNA was available.
source: The movement of the octamer 'off the end' of the DNA, means that SNF2h continued to pull DNA onto the nucleosome even after no entry-side flanking DNA was available.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the histone mapping data showing off-the-end sliding.

claim: SWI/SNF remodelers are well known to be insensitive to DNA flanking the nucleosome, and characteristically slide histone octamers off DNA ends.
source: SWI/SNF remodelers are well known to be insensitive to DNA flanking the nucleosome, and characteristically slide histone octamers off DNA ends (Saha et al., 2005; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: ISWI remodelers typically shift histone octamers to more central locations on DNA fragments, requiring entry-side DNA for movement.
source: In contrast, however, ISWI remodelers typically shift histone octamers to more central locations on DNA fragments, requiring entry-side DNA for movement (Stockdale et al., 2006; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The observation that SNF2h slides octamers off DNA ends suggests that for ISWI, the importance of the entry-side acidic patch outweighs the necessity of available entry-side flanking DNA.
source: Our observation that SNF2h slides these octamers off DNA ends suggests that for ISWI, the importance of the entry-side acidic patch outweighs the necessity of available entry-side flanking DNA.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: DNA length sensing by Chd1 did not appear affected when one of the two acidic patches of the nucleosome was disrupted.
source: In this study we found that DNA length sensing by Chd1 did not appear affected when one of the two acidic patches of the nucleosome was disrupted.
evidence: This is a summary of the Chd1 findings from Figure 2.

claim: Asymmetric presentation of the two acidic patches appeared to dictate the direction of nucleosome sliding by ISWI, overriding the enzyme's normal requirement for flanking DNA on the entry side of the nucleosome.
source: In contrast, asymmetric presentation of the two acidic patches appeared to dictate the direction of nucleosome sliding by ISWI, overriding the enzyme's normal requirement for flanking DNA on the entry side of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is a summary of the ISWI findings from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: For both Chd1 and ISWI remodelers, activation of the ATPase motor at SHL2 correlates with engagement of the DBD on entry-side DNA.
source: For both Chd1 and ISWI remodelers, activation of the ATPase motor at SHL2 correlates with engagement of the DBD on entry-side DNA (Hwang et al., 2014; McKnight et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Chd1 was affected to a similar extent whether a single APM was on one side or the other, and both APM/WT and WT/APM nucleosomes were centered by Chd1.
source: Chd1 was affected to a similar extent whether a single APM was on one side or the other, and although the histone octamers were asymmetric, both APM/WT and WT/APM nucleosomes were centered by Chd1 (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 2.

claim: The behavior of Chd1 is consistent with stimulation of Chd1 activity when interacting with either entry- or exit-side acidic patches.
source: This behavior is consistent with stimulation of Chd1 activity when interacting with either entry- or exit-side acidic patches, implying that Chd1 may reach from SHL2 to entry DNA across either face (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Chd1 data.

claim: SNF2h and ACF had a strikingly asymmetric response to nucleosomes containing one APM and one wild type acidic patch.
source: SNF2h and ACF, in contrast, had a strikingly asymmetric response to nucleosomes containing one APM and one wild type acidic patch.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: ISWI remodelers always moved asymmetric histone cores toward the side with the wild type H2A/H2B dimer.
source: Rather than centering, the ISWI remodelers always moved asymmetric histone cores toward the side with the wild type H2A/H2B dimer, indicating that activity relied heavily on the entry side acidic patch.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 4.

claim: The segment between the DBD and NegC is shorter in ISWI (~40–45 residues) compared with the corresponding segment between the DBD and C-terminal bridge of Chd1 (~75–130 residues).
source: Interestingly, the segment between the DBD and NegC, which immediately follows the ATPase, is shorter in ISWI (~40–45 residues) compared with the corresponding segment between the DBD and C-terminal bridge of Chd1 (~75–130 residues) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The shorter connecting segment for ISWI may limit the path between SHL2 and entry DNA to the nucleosome face containing the entry side H2A/H2B.
source: The shorter connecting segment for ISWI may therefore limit the path between SHL2 and entry DNA to the nucleosome face containing the entry side H2A/H2B.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the sequence analysis.

claim: For both ISWI and Chd1, two copies of the remodeler can simultaneously occupy the two SHL2 sites on opposite sides of the nucleosome.
source: For both ISWI and Chd1, two copies of the remodeler can simultaneously occupy the two SHL2 sites on opposite sides of the nucleosome (Nodelman et al., 2017; Racki et al., 2009; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: SNF2h and ACF bind cooperatively to nucleosomes as dimers.
source: For SNF2h and ACF, however, the remodeler binds cooperatively to nucleosomes as dimers (Racki et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: No cooperativity has been reported for Chd1.
source: whereas no cooperativity has been reported for Chd1.
evidence: This is a statement about the absence of reported cooperativity in the literature.

claim: Chd1 has been shown to dynamically switch between both sides of the nucleosome.
source: Instead, Chd1 has been shown to dynamically switch between both sides of the nucleosome, perhaps helping to ensure back-and-forth motion without an opposing remodeler (Qiu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Chd1 is sensitive to DNA flanking both sides of the nucleosome.
source: Consistent with acting as a monomer, Chd1 is sensitive to DNA flanking both sides of the nucleosome (Nodelman et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Chd1 requires entry-side DNA for tethering the remodeler to the nucleosome.
source: requiring entry-side DNA for tethering the remodeler to the nucleosome (McKnight et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Chd1 makes intramolecular interactions when engaged with exit-side DNA.
source: yet also making intramolecular interactions when engaged with exit-side DNA (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: The strong dependence on the entry side acidic patch resulted in asymmetric histone cores shifting off DNA ends for ISWI.
source: For ISWI, the strong dependence on the entry side acidic patch resulted in the asymmetric histone cores shifting off DNA ends (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Off-the-end movement by ISWI correlated with the creation of free DNA.
source: This off-the-end movement correlated with the creation of free DNA (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 3C.

claim: As long as the entry-side acidic patch is available, ISWI can continue to pull DNA onto the nucleosome even after no more entry DNA is available.
source: and indicated that, as long as the entry-side acidic patch is available, ISWI can continue to pull DNA onto the nucleosome even after no more entry DNA is available (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the histone mapping data showing off-the-end sliding.

claim: The engagement of the ISWI DBD with entry DNA was previously proposed to stimulate removal of the inhibitory NegC element from the ATPase motor.
source: Previously, the engagement of the ISWI DBD with entry DNA was considered to be a key step in remodeler activation, proposed to stimulate removal of the inhibitory NegC element from the ATPase motor (Clapier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: Disruption of NegC largely bypasses the need for activation by the acidic patch.
source: Indeed, this idea is consistent with the recent discovery that disruption of NegC largely bypasses the need for activation by the acidic patch (Gamarra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a published study.

claim: SNF2h can pull DNA ends up to the internal SHL2 where the ATPase motor acts.
source: However, our finding that SNF2h can pull DNA ends up to the internal SHL2 where the ATPase motor acts (Figure 4) shows significant remodeler activity in the absence of entry side DNA (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by the histone mapping data in Figure 4.

claim: The acidic patch is a more important nucleosomal epitope than flanking DNA for ISWI.
source: Instead, these findings show that the acidic patch is a more important nucleosomal epitope than flanking DNA, and that binding to entry DNA is not essential for activating ISWI remodeling activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Binding to entry DNA is not essential for activating ISWI remodeling activity.
source: Instead, these findings show that the acidic patch is a more important nucleosomal epitope than flanking DNA, and that binding to entry DNA is not essential for activating ISWI remodeling activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Remodeling interference can be accomplished by addition of an acidic patch-binding peptide called LANA.
source: Recent work (Dann et al., 2017; Gamarra et al., 2018) showed that, analogously to mutating the acidic patch, remodeling interference could be accomplished by addition of an acidic patch-binding peptide called LANA (Barbera et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Competition for the acidic patch in vivo likely impacts remodeler activity.
source: With the growing list of chromatin binding factors that interact with the acidic patch (McGinty and Tan, 2015), it is likely that competition for this important epitope in vivo impacts remodeler activity (Gamarra et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations.

claim: Asymmetric association of an acidic patch binding factor would temporarily disrupt the ability of ISWI remodelers to create or maintain evenly spaced nucleosome arrays.
source: Based on work described here, we expect that asymmetric association of an acidic patch binding factor, on only one side of the nucleosome, would temporarily disrupt the ability of ISWI remodelers to create or maintain evenly spaced nucleosome arrays.
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the experimental findings.

claim: Asymmetric blockage of the acidic patch could transform ISWI remodelers into disruptive enzymes.
source: In addition, one possibility is that asymmetric blockage of the acidic patch could transform ISWI remodelers into disruptive enzymes.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on the experimental findings.

claim: Remodelers like SWI/SNF that can slide mononucleosomes off DNA ends are disruptive.
source: Remodelers like SWI/SNF that can slide mononucleosomes off DNA ends are disruptive (Hirschhorn et al., 1992; Kwon et al., 1994; Peterson and Herskowitz, 1992; Ulyanova and Schnitzler, 2005; Ulyanova and Schnitzler, 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Shifting a nucleosome into the territory of an adjacent nucleosome is destabilizing.
source: at least in part because shifting a nucleosome into the territory of an adjacent nucleosome is destabilizing (Dechassa et al., 2010; Engeholm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: A modified version of Chd1, with the DBD replaced by monomeric streptavidin, could shift biotinylated histones off DNA ends and disrupt canonical nucleosome wrapping in arrays.
source: We previously reported that a modified version of Chd1, with the DBD replaced by monomeric streptavidin, could shift biotinylated histones off DNA ends and disrupt canonical nucleosome wrapping in arrays (Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The ability to slide nucleosomes without regard for entry DNA is sufficient for nucleosome-disrupting activity.
source: This showed that the ability to slide nucleosomes without regard for entry DNA is sufficient for nucleosome-disrupting activity (Patel et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: A block on only one acidic patch would allow nucleosomes to be shifted into, rather than away from, neighboring nucleosomes by ISWI.
source: For remodelers like ISWI, a block on only one acidic patch would allow nucleosomes to be shifted into, rather than away from, neighboring nucleosomes, and would disrupt rather than preserve transcription factor binding to entry-side DNA.
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the experimental findings.

claim: A block on only one acidic patch would disrupt rather than preserve transcription factor binding to entry-side DNA for ISWI.
source: For remodelers like ISWI, a block on only one acidic patch would allow nucleosomes to be shifted into, rather than away from, neighboring nucleosomes, and would disrupt rather than preserve transcription factor binding to entry-side DNA.
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the experimental findings.

claim: Breaking of inherent two-fold symmetry in the nucleosome can be accomplished through binding of chromatin factors, histone variants, and post translational modifications.
source: The breaking of inherent two-fold symmetry in the nucleosome can be accomplished through binding of chromatin factors, histone variants, and post translational modifications
evidence: This is a general statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Both masking and enhancement of nucleosome epitopes asymmetrically will provide unique strategies for altering the outcome of remodeling reactions.
source: and we anticipate that both masking and enhancement of nucleosome epitopes asymmetrically will provide unique strategies for altering the outcome of remodeling reactions.
evidence: This is a speculative prediction based on the experimental findings.
